newsitem.title: UK: Women, children have special needs in war, doctors.
newsitem.headline: Women, children have special needs in war, doctors.

text.p: Governments and aid agencies have a moral and ethical duty to provide better health care to victims of war as combatants increasingly target civilians, an international team of doctors said on Friday.
The conflict in ex-Yugoslavia especially illustrated how the elderly and women and children were taking the brunt of violence instead of soldiers, they wrote in the Lancet medical journal.

"More than in any other conflicts, the Bosnian tragedy has highlighted how wars are being focused on civilians, and are being designed to break the fabric of society by eroding health and the capacity of people to function normally," Dr Srecko Simic of Sarajevo's Kosevo Hospital and Dr Manuel Carballo of Geneva's International Centre for Migration and Health said.

"The denial of food, water, heat, shelter and physical and mental wellbeing to the people of Sarajevo and the other towns that were besieged for three and a half years has reminded us of mediaeval strategies in which the health and human rights of people were of little meaning."
They said humanitarian agencies needed to focus on health care.

"The notion that healthcare services must inevitably suffer along with other services must be challenged and replaced by one that emphasises the ethical obligation of the international community to ensure continuity and even improvement of services in war," they wrote.
"At no time is the investment in women, mothers and children more important than in conflict and post-conflict periods."
The long-term effects of the war would not be assessed for decades, they said. But simple things could ease the suffering -- and help prevent birth defects, psychological damage and other problems.
"For pregnant women, special food supplements should be fortified," they suggested.
Health professionals should all lobby hard to keep health care in the 20th century. Otherwise, they said, "we will all be party to taking health back in time."
